newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds closed higher on Thursday in very quiet trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.06 pct to 104.24
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 to 103.39
Volume was a moderate 130 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds.

"CPI-linked bonds were mixed and trendless, closing almost unchanged. These bonds have reached an equilibrium and it seems like the market is stabilising at the current level," said Yossi Wiedelfeld of Eyal Securities.

"Investors focused on unlinked bonds which offer a slightly higher yield," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel. "The whole market moved in a narrow range as investors are waiting for fresh news."
The Makams also rose but yields remain unchanged, the trader said, adding that volume was a low 21 million shekels.

Dollar-linked bonds fell sharply after the rise of the shekel against the dollar. In the local forex market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3610 shekels against 3.3700 on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
